author: Georges Andraus
title: Bad experience and support
content: I’ve been using Linearity for a while, and I don’t appreciate the recent updates. The migration from a free to a paid scheme only made the experience worse, making me lose virtually all of my files, since I can no longer export those in vector formats (files I’ve had for 6+ years). The limits to the quality of files, and the obligation to create an account also worsens the usability of the app, since we constantly have to find other ways to backup .curve files. I had pointed these limitations before, and I’ve been contacted by the developer promising these would be addressed. Not only this, but the developer promised to give a free 1-year trial in exchange for me deleting my previous review and posting a new, positive one, but I have never heard back from them since. I do not recommend this app, and other free alternatives outside the app store do a far better job, and don’t put at risk years of work. Really underwhelming to see the evolution of this app.

author: Auroraf0
title: I don’t recommend it to any developer or illustrator looking for serious, professional-grade tools
content:
The Linearity Curve app sells the ambiguous idea that you can freely draw by hand and still export in SVG without losing quality.

The problem is that, in practice, it rasterizes (turns into an image) or keeps the background even when transparency is disabled, which goes against what’s expected from a reliable SVG export tool. The app does not deliver what it promises in an intuitive or transparent way.

I paid for the annual plan and wouldn’t mind renewing it again if the app delivered real quality. I do not recommend it to any developer or illustrator looking for serious, professional-grade tools. After my purchase, I found several other apps with far better value and dramatically better results.
